paras: The shooting of Frank Bowie occurred on a Tuesday afternoon in 1880, reported at the end of August, at LaVilla, Florida, when Deputy Sheriff McCallum shot Bowie, a Black man, in the leg as he fled an attempted arrest. Bowie survived and was taken home for medical care, while the LaVilla town marshal arrested the deputy for firing his pistol in the street.

McCallum and Constable White went over from Jacksonville to LaVilla to arrest four men the paper called "negroes": Sharper Mitchell, George Green, Straph Yong and Frank Bowie. They carried a warrant sworn out by Ben. Alston charging the four with rioting, fighting and assault.

According to the only report found, a crowd gathered before the arrests could be made, and when McCallum tried to take Bowie it closed in, handled both officers roughly and released him. Bowie ran, and the officers chased him with the crowd following; the paper said members of the crowd knocked McCallum down with a club and kicked him in the face. As the chase went on, McCallum fired at Bowie, "fearing the prisoner would escape," and the bullet struck Bowie's leg and disabled him.

The Marshal of LaVilla then arrested McCallum, "the deputy sheriff of the county," for firing his pistol in the street. Bowie got away from the officers and was taken to his home, where he was placed under medical care. The report added that further, unnamed people were arrested and that "the whole matter will be investigated"; no account of that investigation appears in the coverage.

The shooting is known from a single unheadlined paragraph in The Weekly Floridian of Tallahassee on August 31, 1880, printed in a column of brief items from around the state. The paragraph told the story from the officers' side, calling the crowd "a mob of negroes" and giving McCallum's reason for shooting without any statement from Bowie or the crowd. It also reported that the LaVilla marshal "took a hand in the game" by arresting the deputy. No other report of the shooting, in either the white or the Black press, appears in the coverage.

reader.title: Shooting of Frank Bowie
bases: A deputy sheriff shot Frank Bowie in the leg while chasing him during an attempted arrest on a warrant (A1).
Only one paragraph in one white paper, The Weekly Floridian, reports the shooting; no second report or Black-press account was found (A1).

accounts.label: Florida press brief (officers' version)
accounts.gist: A Black crowd rescued Bowie from arrest and beat McCallum during the chase; McCallum shot Bowie in the leg because he feared the prisoner would escape, and was then arrested by the LaVilla marshal.

framing.detail: The Weekly Floridian ran the item without a headline among state briefs, called the crowd 'a mob of negroes' and gave McCallum's reason for firing, but also reported his arrest by the LaVilla marshal and that the matter would be investigated.

quotes: Before the arrests could be made a mob of negroes gathered about the place where the parties were, and when McCallum attempted to arrest Bowie, the mob closed in on him
fearing the prisoner would escape McCallum fired at Bowie, striking his leg and disabling him.
